name: Guo Wu Guan (過五關)
description: Guo Wu Guan (過五關), meaning 'Passing Five Levels', is a Chinese domino solitaire game played with a standard set of 32 Chinese dominoes. The name alludes to the phrase 'Pass five levels and cut six generals' from the Three Kingdoms novel, featuring Guan Yu. Players must strategically remove valid triplets of tiles to clear five levels and defeat six generals.

items.text: Lenient triplets: Tiles removed from a level in step 1 do not need to be adjacent; any set of three tiles in a level that form a valid triplet can be moved to the left end of the common row.

O-Koan (Wu Guan without generals): Five levels of four pieces; common row of 12 stored face down at top. No generals. Remove valid triplets from levels; replenish from common row. Repeat until all levels empty (win) or common row empty with no valid triplet (lose).
通五关 (Tong Wu Guan): Similar to O-Koan but begins with 6 pieces in each level and 2 pieces in the common row.
七擒孟获 (Seven captures of Meng Huo): Single general tile 1-2 (Meng Huo), seven levels with 3 pieces each, common row of 10. General must be captured 7 times to clear all rows and win.
